title: Non-Parametric Optimization for Scalable Learning in Stochastic Decision Problems
claim: Our method reaches lower objectives than the baseline, and its ablation shows the key term matters; it also recovers non-degenerate stochastic optimal trajectories.
layout: 4 plots in a row: training curves, optimal values, two trajectory bundles
description: A row of four line plots labeled (a) to (d). Panel (a) shows objective against update step, from 0 to 5000. SPF in blue reaches the lowest objective, PDM in red sits slightly above it, and an ablation in gray stays much higher. Noisy shaded bands surround each curve. Panel (b) shows optimal value against time from 0 to 1 for Exp1 and Exp2. The solid Exp1 curves for SPF and PDM nearly overlap. The dashed Exp2 curves for SPF and PDM overlap almost exactly and decrease. Panels (c) and (d) show dense bundles of sampled stochastic optimal paths over time. Panel (c) is blue, for x_{t,1}, and panel (d) is red, for x_{t,2}. Each has a lighter 10-90% band and a darker mean trajectory. The paths spread out over time. The eye goes first to the dense colored path bundles.
caption: (a) Learning performance and ablation results for problem Exp1 at t = 1 for the SPF and PDM methods; the ablation curves are obtained by omitting the Malliavin-based term in Eq. (11). (b) Optimal values for each t ∈[0, 1] in problems Exp1 and Exp2. Non-degenerate optimal stochastic trajectories obtained by SPF in problem Exp2 for all t ∈[0, 1] for (c) xt,1 and (d) xt,2.
abstract: Stochastic optimization (SO) plays a central role in decision-making under uncertainty. Among SO problems, time-varying stochastic optimization (TV-SO) is particularly important due to its applications in adaptive control and machine learning. Non-parametric approaches have been proposed for time-varying deterministic optimization; however, they have not been developed for their stochastic counterparts. This work addresses that gap by developing a stochastic variational framework based on Malliavin calculus. This framework yields non-parametric optimality conditions for SO problems with stochastic decisions and supports the design of a scalable deep-learning algorithm that is insensitive to the parameterization dimension. This algorithm, called the Stochastic Path Follower (SPF), is applied to two important problems under distribution drift, namely least-squares recovery and logistic regression. Experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art learning-based and gradient-based methods in both performance and scalability.
